question.text: In the Silver call option example, if the option premium drops from Rs 3,500 to Rs 3,450 over one month (all else equal), what is the annualized Theta?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook's Silver theta example, a Rs 50 fall from Rs 3,500 over one month is (-50/3,500) = -1.43% per month, which annualizes to -1.43% x 12 = -17.14% per annum. The Trap: -1.43% is the monthly rate, not the annual rate. -50% overstates decay and -5% understates it. The workbook explicitly annualizes the monthly figure by multiplying by 12. Note: Theta in the workbook is shown as a negative number because time value erodes as expiry approaches, holding other factors constant.
